preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain control of owner account)
Attacker needs some tokens to perform a trade that will incur high fees

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setBuyTaxes() or setSelTaxes() with extremely high fee percentages (e.g., 99% each). Then perform a token swap through the DEX pair to trigger fee collection. The high fees will be collected in the contract and can be withdrawn to marketing/team wallets (which the owner controls) via swapAndLiquify mechanism. Alternatively, set yourself as excluded from fees before trading to avoid paying the high fees while others pay them.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TokenTool contract has owner-only functions that allow setting extremely high buy/sell taxes (up to 100% total). The owner can also set marketing and team wallet addresses to their own addresses. By setting high taxes and then performing trades, fees accumulate in the contract and are distributed to marketing/team wallets via swapAndLiquify. Since the oracle checks for native token balance increase, we need to ensure ETH flows to the attacker.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate owner, set maximum taxes (99% total), set marketing/team wallets to attacker, perform a trade to trigger fee collection, profit from ETH distributions.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate owner using vm.prank
2. Set buy taxes to 33% each (liquidity, marketing, team) = 99%
3. Set sell taxes to 33% each = 99%
4. Set marketing and team wallets to attacker address
5. Exclude attacker from fees to avoid paying high taxes
6. Get tokens and ETH for trading
7. Approve token spending for router
8. Perform swap (buy then sell) to trigger fee collection
9. Trigger swapAndLiquify if needed by accumulating enough tokens
10. Collect ETH from marketing/team wallets

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The owner has transferred all their tokens, so we can't get tokens from them. We need to acquire tokens through the DEX pair. The exploit should work by: 1) Buying tokens from pair (paying high buy tax), 2) Selling tokens back (paying high sell tax), 3) The contract accumulates fees and distributes ETH to marketing/team wallets (which we set to attacker).
attempts.attack_strategy: Skip token transfer from owner. Instead, use ETH to buy tokens from the DEX pair. Set high taxes first, then perform buy and sell trades to accumulate fees in contract, which will be distributed as ETH to attacker-controlled marketing/team wallets.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate owner to set high taxes and set marketing/team to attacker
2. Give attacker ETH for trading
3. Buy tokens from pair (will pay 99% fee)
4. Sell tokens back (will pay 99% fee)
5. Trigger swapAndLiquify by accumulating enough tokens in contract
6. Profit from ETH distributions
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because the owner has 0 token balance, so trying to transfer tokens from owner to attacker fails with 'Transfer amount must be greater than zero'. We shouldn't try to transfer if owner has 0 balance. Also, we need to ensure we have tokens to trade. The better approach is to buy tokens from the DEX pair using ETH.
